OpenAI just left Azure exclusivity behind.

On April 29, Microsoft and OpenAI restructured their landmark 2019 deal. The result: OpenAI can now sell its full model suite on AWS and Google Cloud for the first time.

This is not a technical footnote. It is a power shift.

For years, accessing OpenAI at scale meant committing to Azure. That constraint shaped enterprise architecture decisions, procurement cycles, and vendor relationships across every industry.

Now, with a reported $50B AWS compute deal already signed and consulting alliances with McKinsey, BCG, Accenture, and Capgemini scaling deployments globally, OpenAI is becoming a platform company — not just a model provider.

For business leaders, the takeaway is clear: multi-cloud AI is no longer optional. The organizations that move fastest to architect flexible, provider-agnostic AI infrastructure will hold the advantage.

The model war is becoming a distribution war. And distribution favors those with the sharpest strategy.
